```{r}
#| include: false
library(here)
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)

config <- yaml::read_yaml(here("r/abrolhos/05_lobster/00_config.yml"))
name <- config$name
legal_size_mm <- config$legal_size_mm

tidy_dir   <- here("data/abrolhos/tidy/lobster")
plot_dir   <- here("plots/abrolhos/lobster")
output_dir <- here("output/abrolhos/lobster")

pots <- read.csv(file.path(tidy_dir, paste0(name, "_lobster-pots_all-years.csv")),
                 colClasses = c(pot_number = "character"))
measurements <- read.csv(file.path(tidy_dir, paste0(name, "_lobster-measurements_all-years.csv")),
                         colClasses = c(pot_number = "character"))
catch_per_pot <- read.csv(file.path(tidy_dir, paste0(name, "_lobster-catch-per-pot.csv")),
                          colClasses = c(pot_number = "character"))
catch_by_zone <- read.csv(file.path(tidy_dir, paste0(name, "_lobster-catch-by-zone.csv")))
```

## Survey effort

Pots were set on Yamatji Shallow Bank in April 2025 and April 2026, across the
Abrolhos Marine Park National Park Zone (no take) and Special Purpose Zone
(open to commercial and recreational fishing).

```{r}
#| tbl-cap: "Pots deployed and lobsters measured, by year and zone"
pots %>%
  group_by(Year = year, Zone = zone) %>%
  summarise(`Pots deployed` = n(),
            `Pots counted` = sum(successful), .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(
    measurements %>%
      filter(species %in% "Western Rock Lobster") %>%
      count(Year = year, Zone = zone, name = "Lobsters measured"),
    by = c("Year", "Zone")
  ) %>%
  kable()
```

Set times were not recorded in 2026, so soak time is available for 2025 only and
catch is reported per pot rather than per pot-hour.

## Pot locations

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Pot locations in each survey year, over marine park zones and 10 m depth contours"
include_graphics(file.path(plot_dir, paste0(name, "_lobster-pot-locations_year.png")))
```

## Abundance

```{r}
#| tbl-cap: "Catch rate per pot (mean and standard error), by year and zone"
catch_by_zone %>%
  transmute(Year = year, Zone = zone, `Pots` = n_pots,
            `Total lobsters` = total_lobsters,
            `Mean per pot` = round(mean_per_pot, 2),
            `SE` = round(se_per_pot, 2),
            `Mean legal per pot` = round(mean_legal, 2),
            `SE legal` = round(se_legal, 2)) %>%
  kable()
```

```{r}
include_graphics(file.path(plot_dir, paste0(name, "_lobster-catch-rate_zone-year.png")))
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Abundance per pot in each survey year. Crosses mark pots that caught no lobsters."

```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Legal sized lobsters per pot in each survey year"
include_graphics(file.path(plot_dir, paste0(name, "_lobster-legal-bubble_year.png")))
```

## Size structure

The minimum legal carapace length for western rock lobster is
`r legal_size_mm` mm.

```{r}
#| tbl-cap: "Carapace length summary, by year and zone"
measurements %>%
  filter(species %in% "Western Rock Lobster", !is.na(carapace_length_mm)) %>%
  group_by(Year = year, Zone = zone) %>%
  summarise(n = n(),
            `Mean length (mm)` = round(mean(carapace_length_mm), 1),
            `Median (mm)` = round(median(carapace_length_mm), 1),
            `Min` = round(min(carapace_length_mm), 1),
            `Max` = round(max(carapace_length_mm), 1),
            `% legal` = round(100 * mean(carapace_length_mm > legal_size_mm), 1),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  kable()
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Carapace length distribution by zone and year"
include_graphics(file.path(plot_dir, paste0(name, "_lobster-size-distribution_zone-year.png")))
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Carapace length distribution by sex. Zone sets the colour and sex sets the shade, with males the lighter bars."
include_graphics(file.path(plot_dir, paste0(name, "_lobster-size-distribution_sex.png")))
```

### Standardised size distributions

Fewer lobsters were caught in 2026 than 2025, so the histograms above are
dominated by differences in abundance. In the two figures below each panel is
scaled to sum to 100%, which removes the abundance signal and shows only the
shape of the size distribution. Sample sizes are given in each panel, as
percentages from a small sample are considerably noisier.

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Carapace length distribution by zone and year, standardised so each panel sums to 100%"
include_graphics(file.path(plot_dir, paste0(name, "_lobster-size-distribution_zone-year_standardised.png")))
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Carapace length distribution by sex, standardised so each panel sums to 100%. Males are the lighter bars."
include_graphics(file.path(plot_dir, paste0(name, "_lobster-size-distribution_sex_standardised.png")))
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Legal and sublegal catch rates by zone and year"
include_graphics(file.path(plot_dir, paste0(name, "_lobster-catch-rate_legal-sublegal.png")))
```

## Modelling: catch inside vs outside the National Park Zone

Legal and sublegal catch per pot were modelled separately with a Tweedie
generalised linear model (log link), fitted in `glmmTMB`:

`catch ~ status * year + depth_z`

where `status` is inside or outside the National Park Zone, `year` is a factor,
and `depth_z` is pot depth standardised to zero mean and unit variance. Predicted
means and standard errors for each status-by-year combination were obtained with
`emmeans`, holding depth at its mean.

The same model was then fitted to legal sized males and legal sized females
separately, giving four models in total. Legal females outnumbered legal males
roughly three to two, and the two sexes differ in behaviour and in how the
fishery takes them, so a change in legal catch can be driven by one sex alone.
The sex specific models are subsets of the legal model rather than independent
tests of it: legal male and legal female catch together make up the legal catch,
apart from `r sum(measurements$sex %in% "Unknown" & measurements$size_class %in% "Legal")`
legal animals whose sex was not recorded.

::: {.callout-important}
## Two limitations to read these results against

**The random effect for site is not included.** The intended specification was
`catch ~ status * year + depth_z + (1 | site)`, where site is the string (line)
of pots. Neither survey records a string identifier, and the 2026 pot numbering
does not follow position along the line, so strings cannot be recovered reliably
from the data. Because pots within a string are not independent, the standard
errors and p-values below are anti-conservative. The predicted means are much
less affected than their uncertainty, so the plots are indicative while the
significance tests are provisional.

**Status is spatially confounded with survey area.** The National Park Zone is a
single contiguous block that was fished on its own day in both years. Comparing
inside with outside is therefore partly comparing the middle area with the
northern and southern areas, and any habitat difference between those areas is
not separable from the effect of protection.
:::

```{r}
#| tbl-cap: "Predicted lobsters per pot from the Tweedie GLM, by status and year"
read.csv(file.path(output_dir, paste0(name, "_lobster-glm-predictions.csv"))) %>%
  transmute(`Size class` = size_class, Status = status, Year = year,
            `Per pot` = round(mean, 2),
            SE = round(se, 2),
            `Lower CL` = round(asymp.LCL, 2),
            `Upper CL` = round(asymp.UCL, 2)) %>%
  kable()
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Predicted catch per pot inside and outside the National Park Zone, for each of the four models. Points are model predictions with standard errors, depth held at its mean."
include_graphics(file.path(plot_dir, paste0(name, "_lobster-glm-control-plot.png")))
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "The same predictions shown as bars"
include_graphics(file.path(plot_dir, paste0(name, "_lobster-glm-barplot.png")))
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: "Observed catch per pot, showing the spread behind the modelled means"
include_graphics(file.path(plot_dir, paste0(name, "_lobster-catch-boxplot.png")))
```

```{r}
#| tbl-cap: "Model coefficients on the log scale. Reference levels are outside the NPZ, 2025."
read.csv(file.path(output_dir, paste0(name, "_lobster-glm-coefficients.csv"))) %>%
  transmute(`Size class` = size_class, Term = term,
            Estimate = round(estimate, 3),
            SE = round(se, 3),
            z = round(z, 2),
            p = if_else(p < 0.001, "<0.001", formatC(p, format = "f", digits = 3))) %>%
  kable()
```

```{r}
#| tbl-cap: "Likelihood ratio test of the status by year interaction"
read.csv(file.path(output_dir, paste0(name, "_lobster-glm-interaction-tests.csv"))) %>%
  transmute(`Size class` = size_class,
            `Chi squared` = round(chisq, 3), df = df,
            p = round(p, 3)) %>%
  kable()
```

Legal catch fell sharply between years (`r round(exp(-1.185), 2)` times the 2025
rate outside the zone, p < 0.001) and was higher inside the National Park Zone in
both years, though that difference was not statistically significant on its own
(p = 0.29). Sublegal catch showed the opposite pattern: substantially lower
inside the zone (p = 0.002) and unchanged between years. Neither interaction was
significant, meaning the difference between zones did not detectably change from
2025 to 2026 — which is expected with only two years of data.

Deeper pots caught more legal lobsters (p = 0.003) and slightly fewer sublegal
lobsters (p = 0.057). Mean depth was almost identical inside and outside the zone
(43.9 m and 43.0 m), so depth is not driving the status comparison.

### Legal males and females

Both sexes tell the same story as the combined legal model, and neither is
driving it on its own. Legal catch fell by close to the same factor between years
for males (`r round(exp(-1.184), 2)`) and females (`r round(exp(-1.182), 2)`),
both p < 0.001. Both sexes were more abundant inside the National Park Zone in
both years, and in neither case was that difference significant on its own
(males p = 0.21, females p = 0.37), nor was either interaction (males p = 0.18,
females p = 0.50). Deeper pots caught more of both sexes (males p = 0.011,
females p = 0.005).

The apparent zone effect is larger for males than females — inside the zone,
predicted male catch was 1.28 times the outside rate in 2025 and 2.08 times in
2026, against 1.20 and 1.55 for females — which is the direction expected if
fishing pressure outside the zone falls more heavily on males. With only two
years of data, neither the sex difference nor the zone difference itself is
statistically supported, and the site caveat above applies equally here.

DHARMa diagnostics were acceptable for three of the four models. The legal male
model showed mild overdispersion (dispersion 1.34, p = 0.032) with no zero
inflation, so its standard errors are likely slightly optimistic on top of the
site limitation already noted.

## Data notes

- Pots that were lost, had a missing trap door, or were flagged in the field as
  not countable are excluded from catch rates but retained in the pot table.
- Pots that caught no lobsters are carried through the analysis as zeros.
- 2026 includes six extra pots labelled `F3`, `F3-2` and `FIII`. These are kept
  as distinct pots rather than merged with the numbered pots.
- Three 2026 pots lost GPS fix on retrieval; corrected positions were read from
  the field comments.
- Non-lobster catch from 2026 is written to a separate bycatch file and is not
  included in these results.
- One 2025 measurement of 24 mm (National Park Zone, pot 2) sits well below the
  next smallest lobster at 50 mm and is likely a data entry error. It has been
  retained pending confirmation.
